newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay court jails Stroessner police chief.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay court jails Stroessner police chief.

text.p: A Paraguayan judge Wednesday ordered the police chief of former dictator Gen. Alfredo Stroessner, retired Gen. Ramon Duarte Vera, jailed pending trial.

Duarte Vera is being tried for the torture and illegal confinement of army Capt. Napoelen Ortigoza, believed to be the longest-suffering political prisoner in South America after being jailed without trial and tortured for 26 years.
Duarte Vera's attorney, Carlos Amarilla, told reporters that the order for his client's detention in a military prison outside the capital, Asuncion, was "an act of injustice."
Duarte Vera was Stroessner's police chief until the late 1960s. He later became ambassador to Bolivia, a post he held until 1993.

Ortigoza and three other army officers were jailed in 1962 in connection with the murder of an officer cadet, in a case portrayed then as a plot against the dictatorship. He managed to escape from jail and flee the country just before the 1989 coup that sent Stroessner into exile.
Ortigoza and his comrades -- one of whom died after 15 years in solitary confinement -- were declared innocent in January.
